Subject: Spike observed: FluxPay p95 latency + throughput drop (initial)

Team —

We saw a correlated p95 latency jump and throughput degradation for FluxPay beginning ~09:45 UTC. Symptoms:
- p95 for gen-api (gpt-variant) rose from ~220ms to ~1.1s across their route.
- Overall request success rate fell ~2.3% (timeouts + 5xx).
- Degraded throughput on dedicated pool behind FluxPay routing (their traffic is pinned to dpool-us-east-1b).

Preliminary signals:
- Node-level I/O saturation on 3 GPUs in the pool (high PCIe stalls).
- KV cache hit-rate dropped ~18% coincident with a spike in short-sequence requests (token length < 40).
- No code deploys in the last 24h. No config rollouts flagged.

Attached: p95_snapshot_may09.csv with per-node metrics and a short tail-sample.

Immediate asks:
1) Markus / Product: do we want to approve an SLO exception for FluxPay (they're on a 99.9% p95 SLA) to avoid an automated credit?
2) Marissa / Eng: can we schedule a 1-hr triage bridge to agree root cause vs mitigations (routing override / temporary cache priming)?
3) Grace / CS: hold off on inbound comms until we vet messaging (pref to give one clear cust note).

I'm standing by to run routing override if we get sign-off (see routing_override_steps.md).

-ben

--
Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Triage update from product/eng POV after quick look:
- Root cause hypothesis: cache-evaporation + hotspotting on small sequences combined with I/O queuing observed on a subset of nodes. There is an upstream queuing regression in the prefetch layer we flagged last month but didn't prioritize.
- Quick mitigation options (ranked):
  1) Routing override to route FluxPay to alternate pool (low code risk, operational risk if capacity tight).
  2) Cache priming job (medium risk, quick to implement; depends on sample set accuracy).
  3) Micro-fix to prefetch layer (higher risk, needs 24–72h).

ETA for cache-priming script: ~3–5 hours incl. validation; I can put one engineer on it now if leadership signs off on doing an exception and approving operational time.

On the roadmap ask: we should add an operator-level routing toggle and a cache-health dashboard (to detect evaporation early). I'll file a short ticket and push for a 2-week sprint slice; but that's a mid-term fix.

If we go routing-override now, we should throttle the override to 20% initially and monitor error rates for 30 minutes before full flip. Ben — can you prepare a rollback plan for that throttle?

-Marissa

Marissa Cole
Director, Product Management
